Subject: PrivGPU capacity protocol: scenario definitions and routing heuristics

Team —

Following the kickoff with Acme this morning, I want to capture a pragmatic capacity protocol we can use for their private GPU pool. Goal: produce a short, operational playbook we can hand to SRE/Acme infra that answers "how much, when, and where" to scale while preserving the latency SLOs. High-level constraints from Acme: sustained multi-tenant throughput up to 1.2M tokens/min in worst-case windows (short bursts up to 2.4M for 30s), strict egress caps per VPC, and requirement for per-tenant QoS shaping.

Key proposal areas for this thread:
- Scenario definitions (sustained, sustained+burst, fat-tail) with sample numbers
- Admission control thresholds and warm-pool / pre-warm handoff timings
- Routing heuristics: latency-first vs cost-first lanes and automatic fallback rules
- Network egress budgeting and batching recommendations

I've attached an initial spreadsheet (privpool-scenarios.xlsx) with candidate numbers and ramp curves. Please review and call out anything we should change before I send to Miriam.

Immediate asks:
1) Laura — please sanity-check the headroom math (token/second conversions and GPU shard concurrency)
2) Vivek — propose admission thresholds and a staged autoscale timeline (warm pool sizes)
3) Jonas — routing fallback sequence and per-tenant shaping knobs (e.g. max concurrent streams)

I'll consolidate and send a short ops-runbook to Acme by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Sergio

Sergio / all —

Quick pass on the spreadsheet: the token-to-flop conversion looks fine for our quantized 8-bit path, but two notes:

1) Sustained baseline: if Acme expects 1.2M tokens/min sustained, that maps to ~20k tokens/sec. For our Llama-variant baseline we model ~12 tokens/sec per GPU shard @ typical prompt-length distribution; that implies roughly 1.6k shards — but with multiplexing and batching we can reduce visible shard count. I've added a "multiplex factor" column in the sheet (tab: headroom) showing conservative (x3) and optimistic (x6) multiplexing assumptions.

2) Burst handling: for 30s 2.4M token spikes, we should rely on warm pools + short-lived burst lanes. Warm pool sizing should target 25-30% of peak concurrent shards to avoid cold-start latency. See my proposed numbers in the "warm_pool" tab.

Action items for me: I'll flatten the sheet into a one-page summary for Acme and call out assumptions. Also attached a quick network egress map (network-egress-map.pdf) showing per-region egress caps and recommended batching guidance.

Laura

Miriam — thanks, good constraints. Quick proposed admission-control and warm-pool plan:

1) Admission thresholds (per-tenant):
   - Soft admit: when per-tenant token-rate <= 60% of tenant cap, route to latency-first lane.
   - Degraded admit: at 60-90%, route to mixed lane (aggressive batching, slight cold-start penalty).
   - Shed: >90% of tenant cap -> apply token-rate throttling and queue backpressure; return 429 with Retry-After or use meter-based token-bucket enforcement.

2) Warm pool sizing and timeline:
   - Baseline sustained lane: provision warm pool equal to 30% of modeled steady-state shards (as Laura outlined).
   - Burst lane: provision ephemeral pool capable of 40-50% of peak shards; trigger via surge detector (90th percentile QPS crossing window). Ephemeral pool must be pre-warmed within 20s for common topologies.
   - Autoscale cadence: scale-up fast (20s buckets) with conservative scale-down (>5m cool-down) to avoid oscillation.

3) Network egress and batching recommendations:
   - Batch target: 8-12 tokens per network frame for typical prompt/response mixes to stay under 12 Gbps given Acme's profile (sheet has specifics).
   - KV cache: encourage local per-tenant caching on shard; recommend TTL=10m for embeddings and prefix cache to reduce repeated egress.

I'll add these to the working doc and provide a sample nginx/router rule for tenant shaping. If Acme wants the spike test next week we can exercise the warm-pool warmup timing.

Vivek

- Miriam / Acme: confirm spike-test window availability (ops+infra will propose 2x30s windows next week)

Routing fallback (proposed sequence):
1) Latency-first lane (when tenant below soft admit threshold)
2) Mixed lane (batched, slightly higher tail latency, lower egress)
3) Cost lane (aggressive quantized variants, routed only if tenant allows degradation)
4) Fallback to degraded response or 429 with guidance (if all else fails)
